newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Nearly 300 Albanians killed since uprising - reports.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 300 Albanians killed since uprising - reports.

text.p: Local media reported on Saturday that most casualties in the past six weeks of near-anarchy in Albania were in the south.

A total of 279 people were killed and more than 598 wounded since March 1, according to press reports citing Interior Ministry sources. The figures do not include an estimated 80 killed when a refugee boat sank on March 28.
The southern port city of Vlore, where the uprising began, was the centre of violence with 60 killed and 400 wounded. Vlore is one of Albania's biggest cities, with 80,000 people.
Violence swept the Balkan state after popular pyramid investment schemes, which were mostly based in Vlore, collapsed and jilted investors rebelled.
The revolt was especially bloody in the south, where rebel committees took control, because many blamed rightist President Sali Berisha, a northerner, for the collapse of the schemes.
Citizens looted army arsenals and seized huge caches of automatic weapons after soldiers and police quit their posts.

Four southern towns were ranked below Vlore on the casualty list: Korca with 21 dead and 35 wounded; Saranda with 18 dead and 34 wounded; Berat with 19 killed and 31 wounded; and Gjirokastra with 11 dead and 18 wounded.
The northern town of Shkoder, with 18 killed and 38 wounded, was sixth.
In the capital Tirana in central Albania, 13 people were reported killed and 64 wounded.
